title: The sulfur-cloud chemistry set and the gates that give it to a planet (GEN.1425)
description: The species the chain may give to an air that has the supplies for them (the Venus chemistry set of section 10 of the unseen-compounds report, V1 to V10) and the numbers of its six gates. Venus is the only calibration planet, so every gate is a physics-supported stand-in and the set is a candidate list, not a claim that a body has them. Nothing in the generator names Venus. Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4).

species.name: sulfuric acid water droplets
species.role: main cloud and haze, the substrate of the rest
species.evidence: READ ([R0157: Table 1] cloud levels and strengths through `sulfuric_cloud.json`; [R3418] the 75 percent index; the curve of `sulfuric_vapor`, GEN.1424); Venus is the only calibration planet

species.name: sulfur dioxide gas
species.evidence: READ (in the gas table; [R5169] fits the sulfur dioxide band, 500 ppb at the cloud top in its model)

species.name: hydrogen chloride, hydrogen fluoride, carbonyl sulfide and carbon monoxide gases
species.evidence: READ (in the gas table and the halogen budget of `mixture_rocky`; Venus's 0.4 to 0.5 ppm of hydrogen chloride is in the Venus acid-cloud report)

species.name: sulfur monoxide and disulfur monoxide gases (and the S2O2 dimer)
species.role: lower-oxidation sulfur from sulfur dioxide photolysis with a reductant
species.evidence: READ ([R5169: Table 3] disulfur monoxide has the lowest misfit of the candidates, 14, and the S2O2 dimer OSSO the best spectral shape, 22; the paper does not detect either)

species.name: elemental sulfur aerosol (S8 and shorter chains)
species.role: haze in a sulfur-rich photochemical air
species.evidence: READ ([R5169: Table 3] S8 misfit 76 to 120 and S4 4e5 against 14 for S2O: a candidate that fits less well, not excluded)

species.name: iron(III) chloride
species.role: cloud-top absorber candidate, needs iron and chlorine
species.evidence: READ ([R5169: Table 3] misfit 86; [R5170] abstract keeps it as the cloud-top iron part, preprint under review, only the abstract read)

species.name: ferric sulfates (acid ferric sulfate and ferric hydroxy sulfates)
species.role: iron host in and below the cloud
species.evidence: READ ([R5170] abstract only; a preprint under review)

species.name: polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons mixed with iron compounds, from cosmic dust
species.role: proposed ultraviolet and visible absorber through the whole profile
species.evidence: READ ([R5170] abstract only: the carbon and iron concentrations of the cloud top need 600 and 3 thousand years of cosmic influx at the least)

species.name: sulfur-chlorine products (SCl2, ClSSCl, SO2Cl2)
species.role: absorber candidate from sulfur dioxide and carbonyl sulfide with hydrogen chloride
species.evidence: READ ([R5169: Table 3] SCl2 misfit 57; the other products are not in the table)

species.name: unidentified ultraviolet absorber, as a measured band
species.evidence: READ for the band ([R5169]: center 0.34 +/- 0.03 micron, width 0.14 +/- 0.01 micron); the strength is a stand-in (L3)

acid_vapor_share_of_so2.basis: The share of the sulfur dioxide that is sulfuric acid vapor at the cloud base, from needed output: the vapor curve of `sulfuric_vapor` (GEN.1424) puts the published Venus base (345 to 367 K at about 1 bar, [R0157: Table 1]) at 3 to 10 ppm of acid in 30 ppm of water, which is 2 to 7 percent of the 150 ppm of sulfur dioxide the Venus acid-cloud report gives below the cloud; 3 percent is inside it. One planet calibrates it, so it is hand-set (L3) until a sweep or a photochemistry model sets it

cloud_water_min_share.basis: The water vapor, as a mole share of the air, below which no standing acid cloud is called: Boss's proposal of section 10.2 of the unseen-compounds report (Venus is a few parts per million at the top and 30 at the base); a floor for a gate, not a solver floor

uv_c_min_w_m2.basis: The least ultraviolet-C flux (100 to 280 nm, `energy_flux_w_m2` times the star's `uv_c_share`) that photolyses sulfur dioxide (190 to 220 nm, section 10.2 gate 3) in enough quantity to make the lower sulfur oxides; from needed output: a young active star at Venus's distance passes (some watts per m2) and a quiet M dwarf at its warm edge (hundredths) does not. No source gives the number

reductant_min_share.basis: The carbon monoxide or carbonyl sulfide, as a mole share of the air, that gives the sulfur oxides a reductant (gate 3); Venus's lower air holds tens of ppm of carbon monoxide. A gate stand-in

sulfur_aerosol_min_so2_share.basis: The sulfur dioxide share above which the photochemistry has enough sulfur to make elemental sulfur aerosol (V5) as well as the lower oxides; Venus's 150 ppm passes, a 1 ppm air does not. A gate stand-in

chlorine_min_share.basis: The hydrogen chloride, as a mole share of the air, that supplies chlorine to V6 and V9 (gate 4); section 10.2 of the report gives 0.1 ppm as the stand-in floor and Venus holds 0.4 to 0.5 ppm. The host star's chlorine reaches the air through the halogen budget of `mixture_rocky`, so the gate reads the air and does not read the star twice

absorber_center_um.basis: The center of the unidentified ultraviolet absorber's band, 0.34 +/- 0.03 micron, retrieved from the MESSENGER/MASCS spectra of Venus's upper cloud ([R5169], abstract and section 4.3, read in full text)

absorber_center_sigma_um.basis: The stated uncertainty of the band center ([R5169], section 4.3)

absorber_fwhm_um.basis: The full width at half maximum of the band, 0.14 +/- 0.01 micron, a Gaussian shape assumed in the retrieval ([R5169], section 4.3); the paper's prior, an earlier retrieval, was 0.33 micron and a width a little under 0.1 micron

absorber_fwhm_sigma_um.basis: The stated uncertainty of the band width ([R5169], section 4.3)

absorber_depth_per_cloud_depth.basis: The absorption optical depth of the band at its center as a share of the acid cloud's depth at 550 nm when the air holds `absorber_so2_reference_share` of sulfur dioxide; [R5169] gives no peak strength in the text (only a figure) so the scale is from needed output (a visibly yellow-ultraviolet-dark cloud), hand-set. The identity of the absorber is not claimed

absorber_so2_reference_share.basis: The sulfur dioxide share of the air at which the absorber reaches its full strength; the strength falls in proportion below it and stays at the full value above. Venus's lower air is 1.3e-4 to 1.8e-4 (the Venus acid-cloud report), a hand-set reference

dust_min_influx_kg_m2_yr.basis: The least cosmic-dust influx per area that gate 5 calls a supply for V8, a tenth of Venus's by `influx.py` with a Solar-System asteroid belt (2.4e21 kg, 2.2 to 3.2 AU, 4.6 Gyr: 1.1e6 kg a year, 2.4e-9 per m2). The one paper that proposes V8 needs the cloud-top carbon and iron to be 600 and 3 thousand years of the influx at the least ([R5170], abstract only), so a tenfold weaker supply stretches those to 6 thousand and 30 thousand years; from needed output, no source gives the share. The comets and the Kuiper belt, the larger share of the real dust, are not in the reference belt, so the number is on the model's own scale
